clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 60s presented with postoperative midline abdominal pain and a palpable lump after elective scoliosis surgery. Initial CT suggested a small hematoma, but repeat CT demonstrated an enlarging small subcutaneous hyperdense lesion in the upper midline abdominal wall. Ultrasound revealed a 2.9×2.1×1.5 cm irregular lobulated hypoechoic mass with internal vascularity in the left paramedian abdominal wall. Biopsy was performed to obtain tissue for histopathology. Although the specific biopsy report text was not disclosed, the final diagnosis references spindle cell proliferation consistent with desmoid-type fibromatosis (DF). The patient had no prior history of abdominal wall trauma or masses and no family history of gastrointestinal or musculoskeletal malignancy. The trajectory is supported by imaging progression of a vascular mass and biopsy confirmation of spindle cell pathology consistent with DF.
